No. Avoid. Take a different teacher. He's terrible. Don't waste your time.

analysis.name: Samir El Omari

Do the homework and come to class, and you will do well.

He has such a sweet & cute personality. He's always happy to answer questions and help. He's a busy guy teaching a lot of classes and he's also an academic adviser. He will always answer your questions during or after class. DO YOUR WORKBOOK work & all other homework and you will do great. Takes attendance but I'm not sure if it's part of the grade

had him again last semester. indeed one of the best prof on campus..I have a conflict with his course this semester but am looking forward to take his course next semester. Such a nice guy. Has a LOT on his plate; sometimes lectures can feel a bit rushed. If you don't do the workbook exercises on your own time, you'll fall behind easily. analysis.name: Jeff Ostrow
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

Professor by far one of the best professors I have had at UMBC, The lectures are clear, he has a sense of humor. Study the Quiz's, because they will help you pass the exam. Exams uses quiz questions(do with that what you will). Learned Oracle SQL , Making EER diagrams, Schemas,etc at a slow pace (so you should be able to get it).

Professor Ostrow is such a good professor. He made SQL very fun and easy to learn. His quizzes are very helpful, they are based off of slides and nothing else. Ostrow is amazing. The online HWs are kind of annoying but mostly because of Pearson. There are in-person lock down quizzes every week but they are pretty simple if u pay attention. Exams are simple. Multiple choice are like the quizzes and the coding portion is open note which is amazing. Love this professor and 1000/10 recommend for any IS class!

BEST PROF! 2 parts of the exam- online MCQ which is theory questions. 2 part is coding- can you use your notes! there will be quizzes before every class from previous lectures to make sure you understand the concepts. Recommendation: read/look over slides before class for quizzes, the book is not needed & for exams review past quizzes its the same!

analysis.name: Rami Quiton
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

Attendance not mandatory. Super sweet and is open to helping with content. Units can be difficult to follow but her in class lectures and activities are the best for learning material. All exams and assignments are online. Would absolutely take her again!

Dr. Q to this day is one of the best professors I've ever had. Amazing lectures. Something about the way she taught made things stick. I don't know. I just loved how organized she was. Everything was set, clear, and precise. You were never under any anxiety and always knew what to expect with her. Come to class and you'll never touch the book + EC

Dr. Quiton is a very knowledgeable and intelligent professor. Assignments consist of weekly check-ins and learning quizzes, 2 reflection writings, and the midterm and final exam. It's a tough class. Make flashcards- all memorization. However, she explains things very well and is helpful. Gives a lot of extra credit and drops an exam. Take advantage of extra credit if you want an A. Go to class, it's interesting and helpful.

analysis.name: Qian Zhu

3 exams, 3 quizzes, few homeworks, one database related technology presentation, and one semester long database design project. Nice teacher. Easy grader. She does not really teach because she expects students to learn by themselves. So it is all about learning independently in the class. If you have time to spare, take this class.
great teacher. very organized. sometimes is a tough grader on homework,but tests are easy. never tests on anything that we didn't go over in class. lots of work, but not hard to keep up with.

I love him as a professor! He is genuinely so funny and he does care about his students even if it doesn't seem like it. He wants you to do well and makes it easy to do so if you GO TO CLASS! Love Dr. Resta! His personality could be misunderstood but he is sweet and kind and loves/is good at what he does. He is a great lecturer. Be nice to him for me you are in good hands

Be prepared to teach all the material to yourself, and only show up when there are quizzes by the end.

analysis.name: Timothy Phin

Probably the best professor I've ever had! This guy has it all. He is funny, smart, and runs a very fun classroom. Take him, you won't regret it.

analysis.name: Jim Thomas

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely my favorite professor at UMBC. You will have a hard time controlling your laughter some days, his stories are insanely funny. There's 3 exams and a paper. He also seems to care about students.
The best professor at UMBC w/o a doubt. Loved coming to class just for his lectures.
10/10 would hear his rants again, only class I would wake up at 8:00 to take

Has a thick accent and would get lost during his lectures. be prepared to do a lot of practice and studying on your own. lectures were always a week ahead of the quizzes. Oliver (TA) provided helpful videos, if you have the indian guy, good luck because he did nothing.

analysis.name: Xiao Wang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Wang's class consists of him reciting the book and if you're lucky, a few exercises not already worked out.  There is a significant disconnect between the weekly problem sets and the book/notes.  His exams are the sort where you think you know everything going in and then are frustrated when you get a C.  Has a very heavy accent.

I took Dr. Wang for Stat 451 & 453.  I would say that 451 is much harder than 453 (because there's going to be less students for 453).  He is very helpful.  However, you have to study really really hard for this class.  His homeworks and test are extremely hard! My advice is better know his office hours for help!

well versed. He teaches exactly what you need to know and is willing to work with you. Stat 453 is a hard subject, but if you are willing to work and show him that you are working hard, you will get the grade you need.
Excellent professor.  Only a few times in the semester was he unclear.  Tough, good at getting students to participate.  You will learn a lot.
Not prepared when attends his lectures and very confusing. Better to read a textbook then come to class. Exams are terrible

analysis.name: Zhifeng Yang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: 3 tests a semester, final not cumulative, graded leniently. Open to questions/helping, provides resources for learning, and seems to care about students. Only setbacks are his accent which becomes understandable as you go to class, and his lectures which can be tedious. Will call on you if he learns your name.

As of my current semester, I think I can say Prof. Yang is my favorite professor I have had for Computer Science. The exams are quite balanced as he gives you great practice exams to prepare you. Also very approachable and understanding. Overall, plenty of resources for you. If you have the option to, please try to get a spot in his class.

Cannot recommend Yang enough. I had him for 203 a few semesters ago and he was incredibly caring, friendly, and willing to work with me outside of class. I hated 203 lol but Yang really is a good guy, passionate, and always willing to help!

Strong teacher, albeit a bit dry at times. As long as you go to class, ask questions, and do your work you'll be fine. If you go to office hours he'll even help you with the homework. Even allows late homework submissions if you have a good track record. Couldn't ask for a better professor.

Clearly one of the best profs ever at UMBC, he is not a tough grader, very open to student feedback, the only reason I did better on the second midterm was because he was recording the lectures, which were very helpful. If you go to him in office hours, he even allows students to work on the homework in the office hrs.

analysis.name: James Year
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: the critiques. i genuinely cried during like 3 of them. he gives a lot of criticism that usually outweighs positive feedback. the assignments were long and torturous (between 100-1000) due every 2 weeks and it's hard to take good pics on campus. he grades pretty leniently as long as you follow the crtieria on the syllabus exactly.

The workload is excessive and unrealistic between 500 and 1,000 photos to complete within a two-week period. He rarely responds to emails. Grading takes an unreasonably long time. Attendance policies are also very strict. If a student is late or misses even one class, a significant number of points are deducted. Do not take this class

ART 211 with Professor Year is a lot of work. The class is split into around 6 assignments that range from 250-1,000 photos each. You only get about two weeks to complete each assignment so don't procrastinate. Grading is strict and missing a class can drag your grade down a lot. Professor Year cares a lot about photos and wants you to as well.

I liked his teaching style and it's clear he has a lot of experience in photography. There is a lot of homework, but not an impossible amount. It will be somewhat harder if you live on campus, since there's only so much you can photograph. As long as you don't procrastinate (seriously don't.) you will be okay!

He gives like 5 huge photography assignments. Every assignment is like 250 pictures MINIMUM and the last few are like 500-1,000. You only have a two week span of time to do all of it. No cropping, all in manual and you have to edit your pictures. He doesn't answer email either

analysis.name: Chunming Yuan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Found the exams online, just memorize those. Nice prof though. Sometimes had extra credit as attendance.

Very nice and enthusiastic professor, and a simple class. He drops the lowest grade for each assignment in quizzes and finals/midterms. All quizzes are open notes, and he allows a note sheet for the midterms/finals. The lectures are a little boring, but he does practice problems and gives extra credit during class.

Took him in the winter thinking it would be easier but he makes the quizzes easy and the exams super hard. Furthermore an A is anything above 90.1 and a B is 75-90 so that was just awesome too. Take 102 with someone else if you can hit if he's your only option just do the work

Very easy to approach, his lectures were sometimes hard to follow but he had notes online that were practically a baseline of the exams. He let's you bring a cheat sheet on exams, so they're never too hard. Make sure to go to lectures because he offers a ton of extra credit throughout the semester.

'Twas the night before Christmas and I still don't have my final grade. He's nice, but the lectures weren't that helpful and were a bit boring. I recommend going anyway for the extra credit assignments. Everything is in the textbook, and the class is easy as long as you study.

analysis.name: Zelalem Yalew
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Incoherent lectures, and when you inevitably cant understand the lectures and need to do some studying out of class, there are no resources available to you except the professors handwritten notes from the lectures, which are just as incoherent as his speaking. He's chill tho not a bad guy just not a good teacher. Avoid taking this guy for sure.

I took CMSC 331 w/ him, not 201. The class was extremely boring and useless. It's extremely theory-heavy. Every class was the same routine. He'd hand us a packet for note-taking and talk for the rest of the class. I could hardly understand his hand-writing. Extremely repetitive and stale lectures to point where I stopped showing up after 2 weeks.

Professor Yalew cares about students' success, however he is new to the department. He is a good lecturer, but it is hard to convert his lectures into usage/implementation without good homework preparation or study materials, which the course lacked in Fall '25. There are hiccups in the expectations and implementation of homework and exams.

I don't think he had the best approach for teaching this class. He would often go very fast, and it would be difficult to follow. While I went to every class, I do not think it is necessary as the lectures are recorded and posted to blackboard. There isn't a lot of homework, but it's 40% of your grade, with and the other 50% being the two exams.

respectful ,open to feedback, very helpful, few homework ,  test and the midterm are the hardest part (most important besides hw) which students should prepare by studying hw, guides , activity problems , and practice . Lectures are clear, handwriting is okay but could improve, heavy on note taking , but releases it online which is very helpful.

analysis.name: Yousef Ebrahimi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Laziest prof ever. Only reads off slides and doesn't elaborate unless asked to. Does 0 live coding. Very hard to reach outside of class. Never gave back our exams. This guy runs the class based off of the leftovers he gets from the course coordinator prof. Unless you have some experience with data structures, don't risk taking this careless prof.

Don't bother going to his lectures; he's a slide reader. He adds nothing of value to the course. Somehow, a computer science class about data structures does neither programming nor proofs. His entire teaching style is "proof by intimidation." The code works because he said so! The proof is true because he said so! Little to no explanation.

He taught really well with clear, step-by-step explanations and a good pace. His lectures were organized, and he used helpful examples that made tough ideas easier to understand. He encouraged questions, was patient, and made students feel comfortable asking for help.

If I wanted someone to read the course coordinator's slides to me, I'd do it myself. I can count on one hand how many times he coded, or put something on the chalkboard.

All of the course material is prepared for him, the guy shows up with his job already done for him and yet he's the laziest faculty member I've ever seen.

Take anyone else.
He reads off slides every class but his explanations are not bad. Good guy, answers questions to the best of his ability.

Dr. Huang has easily been one of the worst professors I have had at UMBC in regards to actually teaching the material. Really easy class, professor taught well for a hybrid course. Easy 2 projects + extra cred project, 4 quizzes/homework, midterm, and final. A breeze. Take this teacher if you can. Quizzes can be found online and were reused from previous classes taught.
She needs to learn how to use a whiteboard for teaching. Also, she needs go back to school and learn how to teach. Unless you can teach yourself stat find a different teacher

You wont need it, just take the class with someone easier.

Very understanding professor, will always work with you, as long as you show you are putting in the effort. Understands the subject well and presents his lectures clearly. Very hard class I think almost everyone was lost. He is a very caring guy, but I think he just has too high expectations. There was a very hard project and he at least gave us a week extension. Very dense lectures, and he's not a very interesting presenter. Only two tests, a project, and 4 homeworks. Tests were very hard, but there was a curve. He's not an outright bad professor and this wasn't the hardest class I've taken, but he wasn't an amazing teacher and it wasn't an easy class.

review_highlights.comment: Professor Young is very wise and kind. Horrible Professor. It is depressing that she is a teacher teaching teachers. She changes grading critera based on favoritism. Contradicted herself in grading on a regular basis. Be prepared to read at least 150 pages a week. Paper due on these readings EVERY week. That is 15 papers people, not including midterm,final, teaching manual, and lesson!

Dr. Young is not interested in teaching undergraduate students. I am surprised she ever worked in public schools because she always talked about how you can't care about the kids. She really uses about the text and makes redundant busy work, for what seems like the only purpose is to have a grade, and then grades strictly, with no concrete rubric.

I think Dr. Young is a classic college professor. She expects you to do the readings outside of class and understand the material. There are a lot of written assignments, but they're all under 2 pages and fairly simple, but she is a tough grader. I learned a lot of the material covered in class and felt as though Dr. Young has really helped me.

Tough class, a lot of readings in the course, assignments everyday. The feedback from assignments are really helpful. If you do all the readings then the assignments are easy. Don't wait to the last minute to read. Midterm & Final is difficult if you don't understand the readings. Overall, she is a good professor. Can't be lazy in this class

She's not mean or anything but shes just not good at teaching and is very disorganized. She read from slides and just doesn't explain well stuff well. Doesn't respond to emails and exams are hard with a very unhelpful study guide. If you're fine teaching yourself everything its ok but you're better ofzaf with a more engaging teacher who cares more.

She was very nice but her organization was not great. Assignments and quizzes were released late so the schedule didn't even matter. She released less quizzes then the syllabus claimed we were supposed to do. Her exams were difficult. Her study guides were somewhat helpful but her exams didn't correlate with the study guide.

analysis.name: Zareen Taj

The only thing I did not like about this professor is, most days she is late to class. She getting into our daily lives and asking about personnel stuff. Other than that, she is a wonderful professor!

Easy course. Went on a field trip to an NGO and gave us breakfast twice throughout the semester. The course consists of 3 reflections, a midterm, and a Case Study paper/presentation. Professor Taj is great. She assigns a reasonable amount of work, is not too demanding, and is very accommodating and willing to help students.

Zareen Taj is an extremely interesting professor and I never lacked to pay attention in class, BUT she is just as happy to talk you to death if you don't participate. So do the reading, come to class knowledgeable in the subject material, and it will go by much more quickly for you as she is beneficially responsive to high participation.

analysis.name: Edward Zieglar
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Although he knows a lot about Networks, he definitely does not know how to teach AT ALL. Terrible lectures. Completely unhelpful when asking questions. Everyone failed all the exams, I'm pretty sure the class was curved 99%. He scans the room every day in the beginning like a robot to see who's missing. Got a 1% and passed with a C. AVOID.

Terrible lecturer. He says to read the book, and class is just for asking questions. He does not post a hw/test schedule online to force people to go to class. Tests and quizzes are impossible. Average quiz grades are 10-20%, and midterm average was 50%. He asks that we read 150+ page chapters in a week, then tests on some very small detail.

Midterm scores were very low, but the grading seemed heavily curved at the end. You MUST read the text for acronyms, he tests strict definitions, not the lecture stories. CPSA HW is confusing until it clicks. Final reused tough quiz Qs. Recovery is possible, but you must study his specific terminology to pass.

Do NOT take this class if you haven't taken Networks or Security. Big emphasis on textbook and conceptual knowledge. Expect this class to take a majority of your time. Not the most encouraging prof, but the assignments and quizzes will make you learn a lot which will help in your career. Relevant information, but if you hate networking, avoid.

Zieglar is by far the worst professor I've had at UMBC. If you read all required material before the lectures & take good notes, you should do well on quizzes. He doesn't make it comfortable to answer questions in class; if any part of your response is incorrect, he will laugh and say "no" 6 times/second. Great material, arrogant professor. Avoid.

analysis.name: Zhiyuan Chen

review_highlights.comment: The homework assignments, exams, and in-class project are all reasonable. Dr. Chen is a good lecturer and it's not at all nerve-wrecking to ask him questions. You're allowed to use two double-sided pages of cheat sheets during the exam. Take anything with Chen!
Amazing professor.  Very accommodating and understanding. His lectures are very clear as well as the discussions. Attend them and you'll know everything you need to.

You will perform well on the assignments and tests if you pay attention during the lectures. Fair grading was applied, and the feedback was very beneficial. The professor answers emails promptly and is readily available for any questions. Anyone interested in taking the course should take because you will learn, and he allows cheat sheet.

Very bland professor. Class is basically 410 pt2. Skip lectures (slides are posted online), and discussions (mandatory attendance) teach you what you need to know. Exams are VERY easy bc A) you can bring a cheat sheet and B) exam problems are based off of the HW. HW problems are based off the discussion examples. Easy class if you put in the work.

The saving grace of 420 with Chen is he lets you bring cheat sheets for the in-person exams. His exams are also pretty straightforward. However, felt the lab sessions were more helpful than the actual lectures, but overall, he teaches decently. Group project takes a decent amount of time - so just stay on top of it.

Excellent professor

I had a really good experience taking this class. Prof. Bridendolph often correlates some of the course material with personal work and designs he did in the industry which made the lectures extremely engaging.

analysis.name: Aaron Massey

Random Lectures. The course is not difficult, he makes it difficult by giving more quantity of assignments and skipping basics. Incomprehensible TA. You will not be able to do any other graduate course work if you take his course.

Dr. Banerjee uses a examples a lot in lecture, I learned more in his class in one week than I've learned in other classes for the whole year. He's willing to help and really wants you to think about good design for mobile apps.

Very nice guy and very good instructor. Slides are very helpful and good study tools. Also not unwilling to curve and help your grade. Attendance is required but the lectures really help. The average on the midterm was low so he gave the midterm again as a take-home test with the potential to boost your test grade by upto 20%. Would take again.

analysis.name: Prakash Bandaru
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: One of the worse IS professor I have taken. This professor has a poor explanation on his lectures. His study guide does not pair with the exact exam, it will be completely different. DO NOT take this professor

The lectures are not too long or boring. Grading criteria sometimes isn't too clear so you may lose points. He doesn't give a study guide for the exams which isn't a big deal but this class has a lot of information so it would be appreciated if there was one. Besides that there's a group project just hope your group actually does their work :)
The IS420 course, led by Professor Prakash Bandaru, suffered from unclear instructions, especially in the group project, causing confusion and stress. Other than that, all was good.

analysis.name: Enrico Berkes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Attend lectures, take notes, do problem sets the moment the day they are assigned so the material is fresh in your mind. Both exams have 11 multiple choice and 2 long questions based on the problem sets and lecture notes. Final was cumulative, 21 multiple choice and 2 long questions

very clear and easy to follow lectures, 12 homework assignments graded on completion with 1 extra credit assignment, exams were tough but I'm also not a good exam taker but if you attend lectures, take notes as they are written on the board, it should be easy.

I took this Fall 2023. He was great! He is great at explaining concepts and if you have questions, he will do his absolute best to answer them. As long as you attend and pay attention, you'll be perfectly fine. Most of the work is weekly homework assignments based on the lecture materials and the exams. Just take notes and pay attention!

Attend the lecture, ask questions, and visit office hours. If you do all of those, it's an easy A. He grades on completion, which means you get full credit for everything. 

12 Problem Sets 
2 Exams 
1 Final Exam

This might be the best professor I have ever gotten, he was so clear during lectures, which made his lectures very important but also interesting, however the tests were a bit hard but if you go to lectures and take notes its an east A

analysis.name: Bedrich Sousedik
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sousedik is a rlly easy grader. Homework, quizzes, and exams are easy A's if you remotely understand the content. Also has a lot of quiz/hw drops. Love this guy, but if you depend on lectures for learning, do not take with diff eq with him. His lectures are boring and his explanations make things seem harder than they are. I recommend tho

The lectures consisted of him just writing the exact example problems that could be found in the textbook. He would teach with his back to the students for the entire lecture, missing students' questions unless they vocally interrupted him. I absolutely do not recommend taking him for 225 there are definitely better professors.

Extremely difficult to follow lectures. His teaching style is to point at pre-written notes and just say the steps of the notes. Doesnt explain things well and is all over the place with his notes and explanations. Tests and quizzes can be very hard. He stated the tests would be based off the quizzes and homework, but they were nothing like it.

Great professor. You can tell he cares about his students. His lectures consist mostly of problems. So, you will have to do reading on your own to understand some concepts, but the concepts in 225 aren't too difficult to grasp.

Hardest 225 prof @ UMBC but you can tell he cares. Grading dist is rough asf tho and the exams (esp Exam 1 and the Final) were more difficult than they needed to be. He also just copied from the book so there's that.

analysis.name: Seungchul Baek

review_highlights.comment: PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Expect to fail because his lectures make no sense and asking questions is of no help either. The TA assigned is no help either. Please for the love of your GPA and money beware of this Professor Baek. Please ask around to see what professor is better and it will be worth the effort.

VERY demotivating unsure what he wants from us. Unsure if we just want to challenge us or wants us to learn. Lecture is not helpful, just practice problems by yourself for tests. Everything's from lecture but students are still struggling. Students can still do well when professors are being kind. Being harsh doesn't always make a good result.

VERY demotivating unsure what he wants from us. Unsure if we just want to challenge us or wants us to learn. Lecture is not helpful, just practice problems by yourself for tests. Everything's from lecture but students are still struggling. Students can still do well when professors are being kind. Being harsh doesn't always make a good result

Never before have I met a more arrogant, inconsiderate professor. 85% of the stuff we went over in class had nothing to do with the quizzes/exams. He was a terrible lecturer. He would put ppl on the spot then laugh when we were confused (which was all the time). Gave out nearly no partial credit on the exam. Avoid if you can.

Very dry lectures that were hard to follow and often weren't even applicable to the hw. However, he would prepare us well for the quizzes and the hw's being a large part of the grade made things much easier. Don't expect to learn much, but it's very passable. I don't recc taking it if you don't have to take it tho

analysis.name: Jonathan Beverley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: New IS Professor for UMBC, has been great so far, he's a good lecturer and has some energy. Flexible, but has a higher set standard, which makes the class difficulty a bit higher than another professor, but its not really outside of expectation for a college class. Good overall, easy to talk to, good overall for his first class as a Professor.

He is really really great! The most engaging IS professor I have taken at UMBC. He really genuinely cares about student success and makes a great effort to get to know every student individually despite it being a larger class. Super accommodating, but still encourages everyone to be on top of their work. Highly recommend.

Class is easy if you keep up with homework and quizzes and understand the textbook concepts. There's a quiz and homework almost every week, so stay on top of it to avoid dropping below a B. The professor is interactive and caring but can be strict at times. Exams are weighted a hefty amount, so make sure to understand the topics well.

FYI on the previous review: He DID curve everyone's exam 1 grades AND dropped quizzes so everyone passed with a minimum B. He's tough on homework and work ethic in general but he is fair and he is understanding. He will work with you if things go sideways and gives you plenty of chances to get back up. For ref, I got a low D in the 1st exam.

Professor Beverley is a great Prof, he made IS 310 much easier to understand with clear explanations and a supportive approach. He was friendly, patient, and always willing to help. His passion for teaching created a positive learning environment. Highly recommend

analysis.name: Robert  Bennett
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors that I have had at UMBC. Wants to get to know you and to succeed in his class. People who end up failing this class are the ones who do not show up to class, it is mandatory!
Great professor. I had no idea what was going on in the class but I wrote  the papers and showed up to class and got an A.
An easy A if you put in the work. Just finish everything on time. Instructions for assignments are on the syllabus and professor can be reached by email.

Professor Beverley is a great instructor! He made ENGL393 much easier to understand with clear explanations and a supportive approach. He was friendly, patient, and always willing to help. His passion for teaching created a positive learning environment. Highly recommend!

SPCH100: Three in-person speeches total. Readings from two books were assigned but not necessary to read and we didn't really talk about them. Laid back class, great practice for public speaking. Don't read from a script, be natural and know your topic. He likes chatting with students about anything from sports to local politics.

analysis.name: Mark Berczynski
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Whether you've been coding for years or you're completely new to it, Prof. B makes his class accessible for students of all coding levels. His playful, banter with the TA's was nothing less than corny, but made the environment more fun than most professors. During the semester coding project, he always uplifted our work and encouraged us.

Amazing professor and a great person overall. His TAs are also really cool, and his COMP101 class is perfect for any new student at UMBC. It provides a refreshing start to your college experience!
Keep in mind that you need to learn how to code things on your own. TAs will definitely help, but you're mostly on your own.

one of the best professors I've had so far. He's funny, caring, and loves what he does. I definitely recommend taking this class, but honestly, he doesn't really teach you how to code; that's mainly up to you to learn. But take this class; he's awesome.

Amazing professor. He was so incredibly kind and welcoming. I was struggling due to family issues, and he completely understood and allowed me more time for assignments. Super responsive to emails(never took more than 24 hours). The mid-term was the only test. Final was a 2-month group project that is VERY easy if you just do 30 minutes a day

As someone who had 0 coding experience, the class was difficult. The TAs helped a lot during office hours, but I needed help with everything. The midterm was long and very difficult. The final group project was hard for a beginner, but my group knew coding. If you go to office hours and show that you're trying, he'll do his best to give you an A!

analysis.name: Anne Bengochea-Cohen
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I love her! She's so cute and really engages the class, which I find very helpful in a language course. She could be clearer when she gives instructions, but she is from France so she definitely knows her stuff. Tests are easy, quizzes are easier. Show up to class, participate, do your homework, get an A. Pretty straightforward.

Dr. Bengochea-Cohen is a lovely professor. She strongly encourages participation and will call on you if you've been quiet for a while, but will guide you through questions if you are confused. She grades generously and encourages struggling students to come to her for help. Overall a very sweet person!

Instructor was very sweet and understood that most people were taking for language requirement. Class was organized and very helpful. Bengochea can seem a little rough at first and will put you on the spot, but is very lenient and willing to work with students. Class is a free A if you make any effort. No complaints.

She is such a sweet, organized, and patient professor. Spent a whole portion of the class reteaching many of the lessons from FREN 101, which helped everyone get their barring's for the units moving forward. Her lectures were very smooth and you did learn a lot more through the lectures than in the homework, but homework is needed beforehand.

An absolutely wonderful professor! Very thorough and uses exercises to help students understand concepts (i.e. white board activities, games, group activities, etc.). She is incredibly sweet and caring; wants her students to do well. You are always prepared prior to taking a quiz and you know exactly what to expect. Homework is fair and doable!

analysis.name: Tamara Bhalla
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Bhalla is a cool person but she has poor time management & gives unequal opportunity for extra credit. The texts are also v long (like a 20 pg PDF which is only 1 of 3 texts you had to read for just 1 class day) & difficult to read. She also races through the PP & DOESN'T POST THEM online while expecting us to know everything on them for exams

i never write these reviews but i just think that professor bhalla deserves more recognition. during these difficult times with COVID, she has been the most understanding, accommodating, caring, and kind professor. she has gone above and beyond to make sure that we are enjoying learning rather than feeling overwhelmed w hw. best prof ive ever had<3

There aren't many independent written assignments (two exams and two journal entries), but there is a considerable amount of short readings to keep up with. None of them are hard, though. There's also a group project, but the difficulty level depends mostly on who you work with. Fair grader. Covers interesting topics. Very kind and understanding.

I really enjoyed her classes, the topics were fun and she really cares about her work, like she is enthusiastic about Asian studies and brings up very interesting topics. I honestly loved to take another Asian studies class with her. I think I learned a lot!!  No textbook but she posts excerpts from books that you need to read!

Best professor I've ever had. Never once did I fear I was going to fail. Just read and do the assignments and you'll be fine. I got 100s on everything including the midterm and final. There were only 3 major graded assignments beside the midterm, final, and final project. 100% recommend. Loved her so much I changed my major!

analysis.name: Amy Bhatt
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bhatt is a great professor! Her classes are heavily discussion based, but she creates an open environment. There is a lot of reading, and then discussing the reading. There is one homework due each week, very easy, and a big research project due at the end of the semester.

Dr. Bhatt is an excellent professor! Class is discussion, she keeps class interesting. Not boring at all 2 HW per week (short reading & response) 1 Midterm & a Final. HWs count higher than midterm.Marks for attendance, listen dont have to pay careful attention since most is common knowledge. Just pay attention & do HW you will get A. 2 Extra credit

Dr. Bhatt is absolutely amazing! Her class is so well put together. There is a lttle bit of everything in her class: 3 Quizzes, 1 Homework a week, some readings, and Final posterboard and paper. She is an great lecturer and she allows for you to learn about the issues from all sides and then come up with your own opinion. Best Professor by far!

HOMIGAWD the class was so easy you literally have to try to not pass. One HW assignment due every week, i did mine all during spring break to get it over with, the quizzes were so straight forward i just looked at my notes the night before to review, but you have to come to class or else you loose points, and she is a sweet lady, TAKE HER

Dr. Bhatt is one of my favorite professors. You can tell she really cares about the subject and wants to get you passionate about it too. Class participation is pretty big and seems daunting at first if you're not a talker, but she creates a welcoming environment and asks good questions to engage students. Easy A if you put in effort.

analysis.name: Divya Bhansali
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I honestly don't see why people are saying this isn't an easy class; everything that's required of you is crystal clear. He's a very nice teacher and uses lots of real world examples to help you understand the concepts better, and as for the assignments and tests, there's  no tricks. He's there to help you learn.

He is a very nice guy and knows what he is talking about. He does give review sheets but it just mentioning what are the important parts of the chaper, so there isnt any questions that you can practice with. He assigns homeworks and gives 3 pop quizes. Also, a huge group project at the end of the semester.

Very nice instructor and a pretty simple class.  Relies heavily on text, but you can really get by with skimming. He hands out a study guide for exams with concepts to study and even notes which parts are most important.  Uses experience and real-world examples in lectures.  Highly recommended.

Good professor but do not take him.. he makes the class very hard to get an A in, when if you take it with any other teacher for mgmt 210 its an easy A. Yes I suppose you learn more but everyone knows you in college for the grade not the actual learning experience..

Mr. Bhansali provides short and to the point PP slides and study guides that tell his students exactly what to study. He sets his students up for success. The test does take some memorization, but at least you know what to study! Highly recommend him!

analysis.name: Elizabeth Stanwyck
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 90 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Stanwyck is an awesome professor! She really cares for how her students learns and is willing to stop lecture to help with questions. She has a great presence in lecture so it's never boring. However, there are quizzes every week but LAs literally go over what's on it right before it so it's not too bad.

Retook this class after taking it with a horrible professor and Stanwyck made the class a 100 times easier. I did WAY better this time around and actually found myself going to lectures, when they weren't mandatory, because of the way shes able to teach. 100% would recommend and she is very nice to approach as well

She is a kind person, but I don't feel she teaches the material effectively. She doesn't always take students' individual situations into account, and I found her approach to be unreasonable at times. The course material is difficult, and the class moves at a very fast pace, which made it hard for me to keep up.

I read all of the reviews for Dr. Stanwyck on here and I thought at first it sounded too good to be true. However, I was pleasantly surprise this semester as Dr. Stanwyck completely blew me out of the water. Amazing professor, was always there to help anyone who had a question. Everyone should take her before graduating, you won't regret it at all.

Liz is absolutely wonderful. This class is difficult and should really be 4 credits, but she still manages to teach well with the time given. She is very attentive to every student and cares about them all. Office hours are crowded, but helpful, and she sends you a copy of all the work done if you go. Homework not graded officially, but do it.

analysis.name: Eric  Bitoude
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Had him for Math 106. He has a rlly hard accent & rlly hard to know what he's saying most of the time. He was alright with teaching math but sometimes idk how I understood what he was saying. theres a lot of hw on a website we did i forgot but omg it was annoying. you basically have teach urself in this class, so beaware its not fun. idk how i pass

Had him this past fall for 115 at Towson, class wasn't too difficult as long as you pay attention. The tests and exams aren't difficult as long as you do the homework and do the study guides posted. Allowed a note card for every exam and did a great job of teaching the material in the class. Even cracked a joke or two during most classes.

Although he was sometimes disorganized, I think he was an overall good professor. I had a lot of fun in his class and I found him very funny. Just make sure to do the homework and study for the tests! He was also a very quick grader. His class was very welcoming, and everyone would participate and work together. I would take him again!

I don't think I have ever experienced a professor like him... He could be very scatter-brained, indecisive and his lectures were very messy. I want to be fair to him seeing as he is a new professor and I am hopeful that he is knowledgable in his profession; I could not understand him at all, the whole class would have to correct him often.

He's a pretty chill professor, and allows a note card on exams with anything on them. His lectures are always on time and organized. He posts the lecture notes after class. Overall pretty good math professor.

analysis.name: Charles Bieberich
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great professor!  Very helpful and cares a lot about his students.  His tests are very tricky.  Just work really hard, go over each question AT LEAST twice, and you should be able to come out with the grade that you want.  He's VERY specific so you can't just memorize the big picture stuff... I got an A by memorizing every little detail I could.
His lectures are awesome and he is so nice and friendly!!! One of the best professors I've ever had. I would love to take his classes again.

Never have I EVER taken a class like this. The exams are designed to make you second-guess what you know, the lectures fast paced, and the homework barely matches the learning objectives. Even with a final grade curve and an exam drop, people still struggle to earn a good grade—take that as a sign!!

The best class I took at UMBC. Amazing teacher. Best Ever. He rocks ! Never enjoyed classes this much (even though it was at 8 AM !). He is super cool and an extremely nice and helpful person. If you are not interested in science, take this class and you will start loving it ! Highly recommended.

Passionate professor who taught hard to understand content in a pretty understandable way! I felt like he was rushing a lot of the time, but to be fair there was a lot of content in each lecture and his slides were thorough enough to go back through and read and understand.

analysis.name: Janelle Billingsley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: 309 has more or less the same coursework for any professor or section however Billingsley does not prepare you for the assignments that are given. Attendance is mandatory and is graded. The lectures are so boring. The course would've been better off online/asynchronous. Heavy work load that's not too difficult but very time consuming

Dr. Billingsley is an amazing professor! She lays out everything clearly, with class only one day a week for the course. One quiz and assignment due weekly with weekly readings. 2 final papers, and a final exam. Love her teaching style and the way she was so energetic at 8 in the morning!

Dr. Billingsley is a great professor and is super nice! This class is a little hard to get through because of how long the class is but I would take this class again with her. The assignments feel like busy work but are very helpful.

analysis.name: Bing Ma
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Best teacher for ECON 101. Really well taught

She's very patient and nice professor, but her class is tough if you don't show up every time and take notes of the lectures. Following the slides and go over the problem sets you will pass this class.

ECON311 is a tough course. However, she really taught well and she was as clear as possible while still making sure you learned all of the information. The exams, although difficult as it supposed to be for ECON 311, were always fair. Highly recommend.

Her style of teaching changed my entire attitude towards her class. Her lectures are a MUST because the examinations are based on the class materials she covers in class. The class has fairly tough exams, but you'll find that the homework and extra credit can level out for a decent grade boost.

If you do bad in this class, it's not her, it's you. Her lectures are crystal clear and she makes the exams as straightforward as possible. This is definitely a less theory, more math type of class but it's really easy if you put in the time to study. Best professor for 311.

analysis.name: Melissa Blair
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Blair is a great professor! I took her HIST 301 class and she is a very nice person that enjoy the topics she teaches. Classes are discussion heavy so attendance is mandatory. Essays and the Mid-Term and Final are based on class discussions as well. I highly recommend taking this course it was very interesting

She is cool, but her lectures are super boring, and it's difficult to pay attention. She is big on group activities. Her assignments are annoying, too. Lots of essays in the class. If you can keep up with the assignments, the class is easy. Participating in class is the worst part.

She is really sweet and caring to her students. Her love of the subject matter carries her classes. Like most UMBC professors, she is far left politically, but unlike most UMBC professors, she doesn't beat you over the head with her politics. Great professor for public history classes. I had her as my adviser and I genuinely miss her!

Prof. Blair is one of the sweetest teachers and I loved her MD History class. Be prepared to write. There are 2 small papers and one big one/ research project. But she does help walk you through the project, which makes it easier. Doing the readings and attending lectures is also vital to passing her midterm/finals.

Very good professor in terms of grading. In my 2 Essays and a Research Paper, even though I'm not a History major she straight up gave me B's. The Midterm and Final is based on the class readings that she assigns, there are study guides for both the exams. Very straightforward and easy-to approach professor.

analysis.name: Edward Birrane
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He has been doing this for years and he is GOOD. A lot of the grading options is up to you (er... the earlier class) you can show up to either of his lectures. He's a really smart nerd with a glorious sense of humour. This is the big one: HE MAKES YOU CARE! His lectures are so good/engaging and so interesting you dont want to leave.

This class has a semester-long group project; your team must find a professor with a project for you. You fill out a lot of documentation, while working on your code. The class material is easy and the reviews tell you everything you need to know. Birrane is a very laid back professor and you'll enjoy his class.

Edward is an okay teacher. His exams had many silly questions and his semester long project was a mess. If you get stuck with 2 group mates who don't care about their grade it's gonna be hard to get an A. He uses a "multiplier" to help boost grades but his algorithm for determining it is ridiculous and many times hurts your grade. Don't recommend.

Cool professor, really smart in his field, great lecturer, and very decent on grading. Pay attention at least 75% in class and you'll do great on the quizzes. Put a couple hours of work in on the project and you'll do well. Material is a little tougher than expected, but for a CS class it's definitely a break.

Great professor with a sense of humor! Exams and quizzes are easy and he tries his best to make sure the whole class passes. Semester-long group project is a pain and the grading was ambiguous at times. He grades them harshly at times. Definitely makes you work for it, but his lectures are worth going to.

analysis.name: William Blake
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Class is 70% self-taught. Required online videos & readings (Perusall) so you're expected to understand the material before class. Disappointing bcs class time serves solely as a review session. Paper on Lochner v. New York—expectations and instructions were barely discussed in class when it is 30% of our grade. Struggles to explain concept clearly

Do not listen to any negative reviews about Professor Blake, I grew to really love this class and enjoy his teaching style. It is easy to succeed in this class but you must be committed and take it seriously. Do the homework, go to every lecture, and study right before the quiz. If you don't like studying or reading, this is not the class for you.

He's strict about many things, the assignments are very clear and demanding in my opinion, and he DOES NOT CARE about the students! He reiterates everything said in the slides on Persuall but then makes attendance mandatory-we don't even review! I suppose it is a good preparation for law school if all the professors there are prudes.

This course is like an undergrad version of law school. There are a lot of readings, and many things we need to know are discussed in class. It's difficult to keep up with the class discussion since he talks about it fast, but he always asks if we need to spend more time on a topic. Not a lot of assignments, but memorizing concepts takes a while.

I like the fact he curves tests and has engaging lectures. There's also only one major essay you have to do throughout the semester, other than that its just Perusals. I did not like the fact that we had lock down browser the exams weren't too bad.

analysis.name: Ryan Bloom
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very hard on grading. Takes a lot of points off from workshop if you do not meet his requirement perfectly. Essays have to be exactly the way he wants. Avoid if possible. Unless you love English do not take.

Extremely tough class. Unless you genuinely love english and appreciate the course, do not take. He treats it more than what a 100 level class should be treated as. Do essays exactly how he wants or you will fail. I went to the writing center to edit my essay and still received a 72% even though the writing center said it was perfectly fine.

This is a grueling class. You won't have fun, it won't be easy, and Bloom will be very strict. Writing essays isn't just a matter of time and diligence; you need a stroke of brilliance and inspiration to even have a topic. Bloom tries to be cool and that's where all the other positive reviews come from, but the class is very difficult.

He is a very hard professor. Gives 3 essays, does not give tests if the class does well in discussion. Very tough grader. If you are not a strong writer, I would recommend finding a different professor. This semester isn't over but I think I got a C, when I am normally an A/B student.
Unless you want to read 300 pages a night and write summaries until your fingers fall off, don't take this class. There are easier ways to satisfy your ENG requirement, trust me. Just don't.

analysis.name: Dawn Block
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors i've had at UMBC. Def worth taking a class with her! Midterm & final is fairly easy if you complete the study questions she gives out a week prior to the exam. Very helpful, funny, friendly & makes the course much more interesting than it really is. Brings in candy on exam days; this semester, she even brought ice cream:)

The class can be a little boring if you go everyday and understand everything. The labs are very helpful in practicing each concept and I would definitely at least flip through the book from time to time. It proved very helpful. Ms. Block and the TAs were very helpful through email. They won't give you the answer but will send you in the right way

review_highlights.comment: I'm really going to miss Conor as it is his last semester here. His class was one of the most interesting and informative classes I have taken. An amazing professor and genuinely the best classes I've had were with Conor. Even if he doesn't teach at UMBC anymore, I would take his class at any institution. Bring back Conor and pay him well!!!!!!!

Professor Donnan is such a gem! If you have the opportunity to take one of his classes you should absolutely jump on it. I took one class of his freshman year almost by accident and he was so amazing that I ended up changing my major to American Studies. His connection with the student body is such a vital resourse for everyone at UMBC.

analysis.name: Marykate Conroy

review_highlights.comment: MCS 144 not MCS 222. Professor Conroy is an amazing professor, if you need to take MCS 144 then take this class with her! Although she may not take attendance through blackboard right away she will eventually put in your attendance grade. MCS 144* She's very sweet and straightforward about assignments. The class is group and presentation oriented, gives a lot of asynchronous days, so you can work with your group and presentations, but sometimes wish we had class to keep people accountable for group work. One group presentation, one individual presentation, and a final interview.

Professor Conroy was great! She was really nice and an easy grader. She kept the class was fun with her presentations and it wasn't intense at all. There is a textbook, but she provides it and it's really small. If you want an A take this class.

analysis.name: Clayton Laurie

review_highlights.comment: Very passionate and knowledgable about the subject (the history of U.S. intelligence, ie- CIA, etc.) Lays out what he wants out of papers and tests very clearly, not difficult, just particular. I would take his classes again but I hear he's retiring.

Lots of work for a 100 level course, but definitely worth taking for a culture credit. It's easy. You can get a good grade on the exams if you go over the practice exams multiple times. Notes during lectures are kind of scrambled, but the only reason to go to class is because he takes attendance and not showing up will affect your grade in the end.

Dr. Laurie is the epitome of history buff. He knows everything, and is extremely eager to impart his knowledge on his students.  The History of Intel. class is absolutely awesome. There's three papers due during the semester, and two tests. He has very clear guidelines for what he expects on the tests and papers; just follow them and you'll do well

I've taken him twice, for hist 306 and 303.  Dr.  Laurie is awesome!  His lectures are awesome and you'll never fall asleep.  He knows everything about what he's teaching.  He's an okay reader.  There's A LOT of reading, though and there's a lot of writing on the test.  Go to class everyday.  I definitely recommend all his classes, they're great :)

He gives out exams questions so it's always helpful.  The way he talk and the way he teaches made my feel like I was living in the WWII days.  Going to his class is like listening to the news broadcast.  Great lecture, very knowledgeable, easy to talk to and work with, defintely very glad I took his class.  This class was one of the best I ever had

Prof Costlow is truly so intelligent and passionate about entrepreneurship. There are no exams this is a presentation-only class so be prepared to present in almost every class. The professor wants students to succeed and learn beneficial material. Very approachable and easy to talk to when working through group presentations.

Professor Coakley is the modern day Yoda For HAPP majors, He is the best teacher I have ever had at UMBC. I'm taking 3 more classes with him. Highly recommended. Listen and pay attention to his notes, he is extremely fair in his tests.

Arguably the best instructor within the HAPP program. Immensely knowledgeable and highly qualified. Very easy class, just a bunch of busy work, but prof. is passive aggressive. I want to be like Dr Cronin when I grow up. He's brilliant in his preferred field of research, sharp and enthusiastic even when stepping outside of it. Dr. Cronin is an amazing professor. He is passionate in what he does and is an awesome lecturer. Couple small papers and 1 very long review paper. Exams were fully written and really tough. No textbook though, so everything is from his lectures. If you're up for the challenge, take his class!
dude, TC is the man!  His expectations are fair even though he can be tough.  He knows so much! He's brilliant!
