Lectures are boring , uninteresting. Doesn't have mannerisms to be a professor, if you ask her schedule regarding questions, sit back to hear sarcastic, rude replies.

Matuszek made the course topics interesting, and is a decent lecturer. The class is roughly half lecture  half group discussion, with weekly online journal entries and a few analysis papers. I'd rather be programming than writing, so I didn't love this class, but Matuszek made it bearable. Not too easy, not too hard.
The course was actually CMSC 691. If you want to take a course with one of the best professors at UMBC, go with Dr. M. You will work hard but you will learn.

analysis.name: Cynthia Hody
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Hody taught me Poli 487 in 1990. Her acumen re: Hegemonic Stability Theory, enabled me to retire from one of the largest Multinational Banks, by age 40, w/ an abundant Pension. I've used her intelligentsia, coupled w my Econ. degree frm UMBC to capitalize emerging financial markets. My suggestion: Pay attention, do the work, & thank her

I wasn't sure about Dr. Hody at first, but I am now taking her for the second time and she's fantastic. She's very outspoken and opinionated which is what put me off at first, but when it comes down to it, she is a super sweet lady who is passionate about politics and really gets to know her students. Tons of reading, but 1010 would take again.

Class is engaging and intellectually stimulating. I knew little about int'l political economics prior to taking this class, but the readings were informative (though at times quite dense); never felt like I was behind in understanding content discussed in class. Liberal bent, but if you are able to justify your position you will be taken seriously

Hody teaches a tough class. She's extremely intelligent and she knows exactly what she's talking about.  If you're not a poli sci or a global studies major, you probably shouldn't take this class, unless you're willing to get deep into international relations.  In this class you will learn a lot, and you will learn to write well. Utilize your TAs!

If you take a class with Hody, expect to work if you want a good grade. There's no getting around it. My grade depended on two things, quizzes and essays. Each essay was 25% and all quizzes were 25% together. I barely clutched a B but only because my essays were A's. You will struggle but you will learn and get better. You will fail 1st essay.

analysis.name: Cynthia Bothwell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is definitely one of my favorites.  She is very caring and makes the class challenging enough so you really know your material.  It can be hard but it definitely helps.  She's very nice and always willing to help when you ask.  She really advocates for her students and wants them to succeed.

She tries to care about her students but doesnt seem to realize that she goes WAY too fast during lectures. Sure, if we were reviewing old material her pace would be acceptable, but when trying to learn new and more complex concepts it doesnt help to have someone who talks to the board and backtracks herself for two and a half hours straight.

This class seems easy, but the way she teaches it makes the class VERY hard and confusing. She moves very fast during lectures and doesn't teach anything that is on the homework. She is nice, but she doesn't know how to get through to her students when she lectures. Since it is too late to drop her class, I have no choice but to teach myself.

She's a great professor wanting to make sure everyone pass the course by giving us opportunities to correct exams and extra credits. However, her exams are pretty difficult - questions on the exam are worded differently than HW we have to do every week. I understood every HW we did 100%, but still failed both 1st and 2nd exam.

I love Professor Bothwell. She really cares about her students and is extremely accommodating. She grades fairly and gives opportunity for extra credit. The only negative is the lectures are a bit fast and unorganized, but she is always happy to explain concepts further after class, in email, or office hours. I definitely recommend this professor!

analysis.name: Cynthia Vagnetti
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I can't tell you anything I learned because everything was busy work. The switch to online because of the pandemic made matters worse. The Professor REFUSED to adjust assignment expectations because we "had all semester to prepare". The group projects were tedious and frustrating. 20+ pages on a proposal about an imaginary issue? AVOID AT ALL COSTS

AVOID AT ALL COSTS! Professor will give very poor instructions and then become upset when students ask her to clarify. She will belittle and degrade you during one on one group meetings, assuming she actually makes time to meet with the group. My favorite is giving students zeros for her mistake, then complains when students ask her to change it.

Took this class FA19 and BOY was it a rollercoaster. There was just no organization. Blackboard assignments were always changing. Students randomly argued with the prof, taking up a good 30 min. Then there's the group project. We struggled to meet the deadlines and ended up with a 47 pg paper. Got an A but was stressed out the entire time.

A WI class with LOTS of HW/CW. Prof often gave group project work + solo essay project work + mini hw that just felt tedious for the purpose of being tedious. Criteria often vague, and if you miss 1 assignment , good luck, bc it snowballs and it is very easy to be swallowed up with work. If you're an IS major, just take IS 369 if you can

THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER. PLEASE DON"T TAKE HER CLASS. For a technical communication writing professor, she is TERRIBLE. She does not provide CLEAR instructions, and she has the biggest ego out of everyone in class. Question her and she will belittle you.

analysis.name: Joan Davenport
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Joan is problematic. She yelled and belittled students them in the front of the entire class, and has been known to do the same with faculty, too. While that doesn't meet the school's values of respect, there's been a lack of accountability (another value that's not upheld). Different race, different standards.

Dr. Davenport will appear to be "too cool for school" as the last rater described her, but she is definitely not out to help students succeed. Especially, CERTAIN students. I will just leave that to your imagination. Read the book, do the lab book, and pray you get a good clinical instructor, who can give you the practical experience to learn.

Prof Davenport seems very nice in class, but her lectures do not prepare you for the exams at all! It seemed like no matter how hard you study, the exams felt impossible and it almost discouraged me from studying because studying didn't seem to help. She is a very harsh grader, and you will basically need to teach yourself the content. Not good

Yes very lively lecturer but can also be very unprofessional/rough 2 students by embarrassing them in front of class if they say something stupid. She picks on people in the front row 2 do assessement on in front of whole class. Lectures do not cover what's on tests. Use book & wkbk. Prep for Val #4 from Day 1 & it will help prep 4 exams 2.

Shes pretty entertaining but like everyone else said, you HAVE to read the book. Attending class isnt important (as long as you read), but it isnt super painful either - she's interesting. Focus on LAB! You can really learn a lot there that is helpful for the tests if you don't just mess around the whole time.

analysis.name: Daniel Jenkins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great guy - very funny and makes what I consider to be a dry subject very interesting. Lots of reading but don't worry, he goes over everything in class (so if you don't read or didn't understand you won't miss much). Only exams and a final paper (plus attendance grade), but if you do his study guides and ask questions the exams aren't bad at all

3 fairly hard (open note) exams but had the option of averaging first 2 for a grade on the 3rd. 1 paper. Attendance is mandatory and there are a lot of readings, but I think the discussions and lectures are worthwhile for learning the material. He is pretty funny as well and tells stories about his experiences which he ties back into the material.

He's a decent lecturer, but he doesn't use slides so reviewing for exams is a bit tedious and it's hard to know what exactly his grading criteria is. Not all readings are used in exams or even discussed in class, and there are 7+ readings per week, so keeping up sometimes feels like a waste of time. Interesting content though!

Great professor! Took this course completely asynchronously and had no trouble at all, he's a proficient grader as well. As a freshman in my first semester, the course was interesting and easy to follow, definitely recommend taking it with him!

He is a really good professor. PHIL 152 was super easy. He makes a study guide for all exams and goes over it in class. He averaged the first two exams and if you had a passing grade you did not have to take the 3rd exam if you did not want to- you just automatically receive the average grade of the first 2 exams for your third exam grade.

analysis.name: Daniel Gonzales
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of my favorite professors in the physics department! He cares deeply about his students and is ALWAYS there for help. I found the lectures were extremely useful for completing the lab reports. Also, even though lab is 3 hours, it never actually takes that long. You can tell he genuinely enjoys what he does and wants to see his students thrive.

He is very understanding to students and clearly loves what he does. He enables you to succeed and is very accessible & approachable. As with all lab classes, the lab reports take time, and it's never something to procrastinate on as you will not have enough time otherwise. But he gives the most digestible & pleasant experience for such a class.
Very good prof, you can tell he cares a lot about his students. The class was a lot of work at times but as long as you do the work and listen to grading feedback it's not that hard to get an A.

Lectures are skippable if you know your statistics and physics 2. Labs are pretty interesting and usually we finished with 2 hours to spare, you must do a report for every lab but you get two weeks to do them. Very lenient grader on the final project and he brought snacks on presentation day. He's awesome and I love him. Makes a lab class fun.

One of the best professors in UMBC. I've been in this university for quite a while and can with confidence say that Dr. Gonzales is one of the most kind, caring, and smart professors out there. He always listens to student feedback and gladly helps with things unrelated to his class, be it other homework or life advice. Everyone I know loves him:)

analysis.name: Radhi Datla
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She has a very traditional way of teaching. Being in her class made me feel I was back home. Other then that she is a nice person but can be strict. Do the assignments and study and you should be fine. Also make sure to pay attention in class because she WILL call on everyone 1-3 times a class.

Overall a decentish professor however she WILL call on you in class so pay attention. It's not too difficult, usually around 2-3 assignments due thursday night. No final exam, instead multiple 3 big tests throughout the semester. Also multiple quizzes.

as a 4 credit class she DOES in fact challenge students so be ready to be called on and have lots of hw.
She is a hard professor but she is a nice person

As a person who is FLUENT in Hindi, this course was very difficult. She wants your camera to be on during class and she requires that you participate by randomly calling on people to read/speak. I would try to take another language if I were you, because again, even as a native speaker this class was stressful. Also, points off for anything small.

Would not recommend taking Hindi with her if you are not familiar with reading/writing in Hindi (she does not treat this class like an Intro to Hindi). Homework is worksheets from the textbook (fairly easy), but quizzes were dictation (really difficult). She also will call on EVERYONE in the class, so you have to be paying attention/participating.

analysis.name: Sanorita Dey
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures were comprehensive for the topics, she will answer questions if any students have any. The class projects are not made by her however and tend to be very difficult to code. Her exams are easier than the other professors and doesn't assign homework. Don't let this fool you as there is no point buffer because of no homework. Study!!!

Overall chill professor, would recommend attending lectures in person because notes are handwritten and difficult to understand. Exams are relatively easy if you pay attention during lecture. Is very engaging and encourages students to ask questions. Responds to emails very quickly and is accessible outside of class.

Prof Dey gets a bad rep but in all honesty she does the best she can. All 341 Profs will suck bc the class is hard. She tries to be understanding and has extra credit opportunities, she doesn't swarm you with HW bc projects are already hard. Her tests are not difficult as long as you either study well or go to class. She's a great prof just try.

She writes on a chalkboard, which makes it easy to take notes. She grades leniently; I thought I failed an exam once only to get a B. Projects not by her. Lectures are important or you'll get lost; Notes aren't the clearest. Very understanding and gave me project extension when I had family emergency. +4% extra credit overall. Only teaches in fall.

Def. take her for CMSC 341 her explanations are spot on! Uses chalk to draw examples on board and knows the content and wants the student to actually learn. Attendance was not mandatory but i still attended each class b/c of how the amount of content she covered in each class with thorough explanations. Responds pretty quickly too on emails. Chill

analysis.name: MaryAnn Davenport
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Davenport is knowledgeable and fair, and offers extra credit throughout the semester. Understands that we may have other tougher classes to worry about, she keeps class simple, interesting, and engaging. I got a C due to personal circumstances, but she is a great professor and the class is not difficult.

Definitely one of the best professors I have very taken. Accounting can be a difficult subject, but she gives an easy understanding to each chapter's content. Read and do the homework before class and compare your answers to hers and ask questions about any differences.

Good prof. Very supportive of my struggles outside of school. Prof is very funny and made class fun. However, exam 2 and final exam were kind of difficult and I did poorly on both of them which dropped my grade down to a C.

There is little that I need to say that hasn't already been said about professor Davenport; she has undoubtedly earned her 5.0 rating. Her classes are very hands on, and she is very clear on which topics she expects you to understand and which she doesn't. Her class made this econ major very interested in further pursuit of accounting.

Professor Davenport was one of the best teachers I've ever had at my time at UMBC. She is very understand and you can tell she's very passionate about her class and she loves her job. The workload is not difficult at all and there are no exams. GREAT TEACHER AND GREAT CLASS! YOU WONT REGRET TAKING THIS CLASS!

analysis.name: Deepa Madan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: So sweet and caring, genuinely cares about her students. Grading is super generous compared to other professors in the department. Getting an A in this class is very realistic in this class
Great proffessor. Can sometimes be very repetitive, but she knows her stuff. Also a fashionista at heart.
Generous grading, caring and friendly prof

Prof Madan is fairly good. She was just okay at explaining new things and used class time to just go over a bunch of examples. The best part of the class was what you were expected to understand. Deadlines were clear and the tests were very representative of the material studied. TA was pretty bad. Took partially online during COVID crisis
Incredibly nice. She is very approachable and is of great help in office hours. If you understand all of the homework and lecture slides, you will do well in this class.

analysis.name: Deepinder Sidhu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The book is a better teacher than this professor +when directly questioned, he will explain concepts -teaches surface level overviews and expects students to know complex material -does not disclose topics or units covered on exams and tests until 3 days before the exam at the earliest -exams graded based on nitpicking & minutia, not understanding

Worst professor I have ever had by far! Not easy to understand, speaks in a monotone, incredibly boring material being presented by a incredibly boring professor. No textbook so the only way to learn is to listen to him. Terrible. Just awful. Booooooo!

Laziest professor at UMBC. No textbook. No slides. Leaves immediately after class. I felt like I had no resources to learn. Sidhu is good at teaching and the TA is decent, but I need a text or slides or something. He goes way to fast to write it all down. Lenient grader. This class is 80% memorization. Helpful to record lecture. Wiki is your bff.

This was my second class with professor Sidhu. This class was a complete waste of my time. In an attempt to avoid teaching the class himself, he makes students give group presentations every day. This means each student gives one presentation per week. He gave vague input on the presentations and was upset they were low quality. Go figure....

Sidhu doesn't care, at all. The entire class is just your team working on a semester long project, which is anything of your choosing. At the end, you turn in a small project report, and present your project to the class. Everything is peer graded. Just avoid this guy. He won't teach you anything, and showed up only half the time, maybe less.

analysis.name: Deepak Koirala
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is one of the best professors in the Chemistry department! He made the information easily digestible and was very clear in his expectations. I'm not a big fan of chemistry but he made me love the class. The topic is not easy but honestly, put some effort in and you will be fine. He's very understanding and he wants us to succeed!
he is very sweet and his lectures were good, he tends to ramble though so you might get lost. lectures are helpful to come to. expecations on quizzes and exams are very clear

Dr. Koirala is extremely kind and caring and is very willing to help other students outside of class. The lectures are very clear and he gives practice problems that very closely resemble the quizzes/exams. Extra credit questions on quizzes were also very easy. Lectures can be a bit boring at times cause he can overexplain things.

Take this bichem class with him and Aaron smith! His first half was really good he made things very understandable and you can always email him if you didnt understand a topic. He is a little monotone so lectures can be boring sometimes esp for the 2 hours of class, but his exams are not hard if you study and he made biochem easy to remember.10/10

His lectures were mostly him reading off the slides which made it useless to attend lectures. He was not engaging in presenting the information. He did have a lot of practice in between the slides which were helpful, especially since the quizzes and exams were exactly like the practice.

analysis.name: Dhananjay Phatak
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Extremely arbitrary grader. If you show up to exams and labs, you are guaranteed to get a B. There is no question about it. The exams are extremely difficult, but he claims to curve the exams. In reality he doesn't curve the exams, but you will still end up with a B. If you want an A sit in the front row and ask questions. The lectures are useless.

Grade depends on labs, 2 midterms, final. Allows cheat sheets. Heavy accent, goes on tangents. Remembers names, likes to call on people. He will tell exam material in class & review sessions. Talk to the TAs in discussions! Go to labs! Exam avg in 30s, 3-4 problems, more complicated than examples he'll do. B/c curve, I needed 25% overall for a B

Where to begin? He gives grades by flipping a coin. I landed on the 'B' side and I could get past that easily. However, when I showed up in CMPE310 after 212, I was so far behind because he didn't teach us a single thing. He also didn't really care about us too much because he's a research prof and we aren't research so we aren't worth his time.

Phatak understands the material, but doesn't know how to teach it very well. His lectures are very muddled. His tests are very hard, but he curves them very heavily, and most people end up with a B in the class if they put some effort into the class.

His lectures are confusing and unclear. He speaks extremely fast, making it hard to understand him. When he learns a student's name, he calls them out, randomly selecting them to answer questions that no one knows the answer to. His test averages hover somewhere around a 30%, which he claims is intentional. Keep in mind 212 is a gateway for COMPE.

analysis.name: Dennis Coates
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His Lectures are ok because they provide handy, straightforward notes even though the lecture is almost 3 hours long. His online quizzes (multiple choice) are hard at the start but become really easy after quiz 3. Study HIS OLD EXAMS they are the key to passing his class especially how heavy the midterm and final are. HE IS BETTER than Prof Maria!!

An awfully hard class and the professor's lack of structure + bad attitude make it worse. To succeed, take notes from the slides before class because there's no clear syllabus or outline. Don't expect guidance the professor discourages using the textbook and offers no organized materials, DONT LISTEN TO HIM USE ONLINE RESOURCES if you want to pass!

MUST go to class since the lectures are very loosely based on the textbook and no notes are uploaded. Gives old exams to look at which are very helpful for the midterm and final, and the final is weighted heavily, although the class is points-based which is great. Hard to sit thru for 2 1/2 hrs but it'll pay off

Professor Coates is a very nice and accessible professor. There are weekly discussion posts and quizzes, the quizzes are very difficult but discussion posts are free 100% so make sure to do those. Then, there are four papers which are easy money. Lectures are extremely boring but necessary to complete quizzes. Go to class and this course is cake.

Very bland and monotonous lectures. He'd previously used powerpoints to help but for some reason ditched those in favor of scribbling on a whiteboard with confusing symbology & messy handwriting. Med. score on first exam was 40%, refused to curve. Textbook differs from quizzes & exams. Old exams on BB but wouldn't put up a key to help with review.

analysis.name: Lisa Dickson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: hard to hear her. her is laugh is unbearable. its like a annoying evil laugh. she is not understanding at all. talks about her husband a lot. she makes an easy class super hard.

Lisa is a nice person and is approachable if you need help. However, her teaching style is pretty bad for microeconomics. She rushes through material and doesn't explain concepts well. Had 3 tests during semester and she makes up all questions so be ready to teach yourself the material alot.

Alright class. Managed to get an A fairly easily, but she gives out a ton (more than I've ever seen) of different readings which you're expected to understand for the exams. Not hard, but a good bit of material. She doesn't give great feedback and takes forever to grade things. It's an alright class as long as you take notes and study a bit.
She flat out does not know how to teach. Lectures are very dry. Does drop the lowest quiz and HW grade, however.

Prof. Dickson is a great professor. She's passionate about economics and tries her best to make it interesting. The homework is on Pearson with unlimited tries, the quizzes are easy, just do the homework and read your notes. She goes over past topics a lot and makes the topics easy to understand. Attendance isn't required but it's suggested.

analysis.name: Lindsay DiCuirci
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Teaches super well and easy to learn material. No exams but projects instead and attendance matters.

Very outgoing and caring. She gives very detailed feedback on your papers/projects and even if you have major mistakes, she doesn't take off many points for it as long as you show effort. She'll ask you to get 2 books, one about printing and leaves of grass. Only get leaves of grass. Lot of the readings you can skip

This class was very easy and honestly you can get by without doing some of the readings as long as there's no work to go with it. There are some papers but very little of them can't be done within an hour. Professor DiCuirci is great and passionate about what she does and I would love to be in another one of her classes.

Great professor, very understanding and social towards her students. She didn't give out large amounts of work and is very lenient on her grading. She gives great advice so if you apply it for your next paper/project you will surely receive a better grade

She's great. She's nice, intelligent, and kept my attention the entire class: even if it got a little stale. Typical two papers, midterm, final, some quizzes and a participation grade. She loves participation too. Take her and you won't regret it.

analysis.name: Maria Guimaro Diniz Cambraia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment:
We're given prequizzes to watch before units like Phys, Bio, etc. Next, with group, do a protocol sheet where you hypothesis & write how you will do your experiment. Then, do experiment. Lastly, you record results. You're given HW too. Extremely easy class (HS lab course).

Only bad side is professor talks alot, which hinders from doing expriments.

Dr. Cambraia is one of the best teachers I've ever had! She's very sweet and is always willing to help anyone! Felt like I learned more from her than my intro chem lab. Wish she taught more classes! Assigned lab reports, but gave extensions if you asked. Genuinely wants students to learn and succeed! Definitely take her is you have the opportunity!

Microbiology is a class you have to study for. She makes it bit bearable and it is possible to get an A if you put in the work. We work with groups a lot in this class but as someone that hates group work, it is definitely not bad. She is funny and helps outside of class if you ask. Definitely love her class! 100% recommended.

analysis.name: Thania Munoz Diaz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: i love prof munoz!!! literally the best professor at UMBC, so sweet and caring. she is very understanding that you have other obligations outside her class she is very lenient. her class consist of reading the assigned readings and talking about them, a few quizzes and a group and solo project. if you know spanish you will get an A. def reccomend!
Great professor. was amazing at teaching and kept thing clear simple and fun. If you know Spanish already easy A

She is a very nice teacher if something is happening with you, she will help you out and even give you more time if you are overwhelmed. Tip for quizzes the day before a quiz ask her what to study sometimes the quizzes are questions, we have done in class.

Muñoz is new, but amazing. She is extremely helpful and wants the students to do well. Very fair grader. She's extremely intelligent and assigns some difficult readings, but isn't pretentious or patronizing. She is overall an amazing professor and made the semester a lot better. Oh yeah, she's beautiful, too!

There was plenty of work but it was nothing crazy and she was very flexible about due dates if you talked to her. She gives great feedback on essays and other work, and wants to make sure you know the topic before quizzes or exams. She was really a wonderful professor.

analysis.name: Jeremy Dixon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Lectures not helpful, not understanding about grades, exams based off slides so reading the book doesn't really help. Would not recommend.

His powerpoints and lectures are good, but his interactions with students are horrendous. When helping students, he is very condescending and patronizing. The project guidelines are oftentimes misleading and confusing, but professor Dixon's attitude towards students discourages them from asking questions and actively seeking help.

Good lecturer stuck in a badly designed course. Exams written by other professors did not match what was taught. Writing code on paper in 2025 is outdated and unfair. Email responses were slow or nonexistent. The teaching was solid. The system around it failed.
He unnecessary makes projects very difficult and tells us to use functions that we haven't covered in lecture yet. Doesn't show all sample outputs on project handouts.

HORRIBLE PROFESSOR. literally had PROOF of not working on a file after the submission and didnt submit because the submission instruction was WRONGG!!!!!!!! AND NOW CANT EVEN GET CREDIT FOR THE WORK????? THERES EVIDENCE AND THIS PROFESSOR CANT ADMIT HIS MISTAKES AND JUST BE FAIR FOR HIS OWN ERROR. Guys stay away, PLS FOR YOUR SANITY.

analysis.name: Dina Glazer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Study and do the required readings and you will do well. I am surprised to see the poor ratings, the professor is more than willing to help after class and the networking knowledge (mainly concepts in 451)  is very valuable. The IS people who complain the technology classes are too hard (We have it easy compared to comp sci) should switch to BTA.
Exams are extremely hard, nothing from her notes help. Boring lectures

IS 450: class was a nice 450 experience. HW every week, not too hard. 3 exams, non-cumulative final. She reviews your study guide and gives suggestions if you send it early enough. Lectures are pretty boring. Wireshark labs weren't too hard. In-class exercise every once in a while, that is graded, so don't skip too many lectures. She's very nice.

Horrible Professor- If you do not have a background in Networking her tests are impossible. She will not help you study for material that is going to be on it. She is not helpful when you ask outside of class. DO NOT TAKE THIS UNLESS YOU HAVE A STRONG NETWORKING BACKGROUND.

Solid prof. 3 non-cumulative in-person tests, ~9 HWs (on blackboard & timed, 1 dropped). Lectures are ok, slides posted online with some extra readings. HWs are straightforward as long as you review the slides/readings. Exams are so-so; can easily catch you off guard if you don't prep; lets you send in your study guide and will give feedback on it.

analysis.name: Dorothea Johnson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I had Mrs. Johnson for both AGNG 200 + 320. Class is in Python as of 2025 fall

Homework is almost weekly, you have to solve 5 coding problems for homeworks

He is very knowledgeable and always eager to share it with you (as long as it's during office hours... "teaching is a job!").  Don't fear, just man up.  You'll be a stronger person if you survive.

Smart. Extrmly tgh grdr. You could spnd 12 hrs on a reprt, it's perfct, you get a 90 b/c he didn't lik th ordr or choice of wrds in 1 sent.  He goes vry fst, somtims dsn't use exmpls when nec.  Exms are hard and some ?s arnt taught, & not in txt, reqr resrch or extrpltn of fcts. lern lots thogh. Smtmes it's hard to c how infrmtn is going 2 b used

He lectures better than any other professor in the department.  There is a final project where you have to build a toy (yes, another toy project) that is run off of elastic or potential energy.  There are also labs where you use a milling machine and a lathe.  Take lots of notes, but still you'll need a miracle to get a B on any of his exams.

Very knowledgeable on a subject, never had a lecture prepared on a sheet of paper, derived every formula from memory and all lectures were organized as though he were reading from a script. Talks and writes at the same time, bring a recording device and write at the same time. Ruthless taskmaster, be warned. He will insult your intelligence.

analysis.name: Shelter Dziya
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class structure under her supervision is easy because most of the material was kinda common sense so class lecture is very boring, I fell asleep a few times but still got an A because last minute reading is sufficient. Exams were online for this semester and open note so the course is a breeze. She reads off the laptop so its all book stuff.

Professor Shelter Is passionate and dedicated. She's consistent in her expectations and clear in her requirements. If you engage and put in work she'll work with. No chance of coasting and passing, she won't make last minute exceptions if you've not engaged throughout. Good sense of humour and inspirational. Her motivation motivates!

Shelter Dziya is a very compassionate lecturer, she truly does care about student well being, i was going through a tough time with some family matters and she took the time to email and check in on me. The lectures are clear, enjoyable and i feel that i have managed to get alot of of them.

I expected this to be an easy class because its a 100 level. I am also a junior so I didn't expect the class to have such strict participation and attendance rules. Aside from that the professor was really fun and engaging. Some topics were better than others but for the most part I really enjoyed this course. Just wish attendance wasn't mandatory.

She tried to fail me because I missed a test, for which I was in the hospital at the time. I've seen her google the answers to questions she is asked during the middle of class. To top it off, none of the study material she gives out is actually her own work. One of the most asinine professors I've ever had. Astounded that she is employed at UMBC.

analysis.name: Susan Dwyer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's a great teacher.  She's so funny and makes the class interesting -- and her Australian accent is so cute!  I had a death in my family when the final paper was due and she was so understanding and really helped me out.  She's always willing to talk or help you out if you stop by her office after class.  The class is a challenge but very fun!
One of the best profs i've had. Shes very nice and helpful. She even helped me do a project for another class. Very interesting subject matter.

The class was really good! She lets you get into debates with your classmates which I found really helpful when it came time to write my final schema analysis. She expresses her own view a lot...but if you can get beyond that, she's a lot of fun!!

Interesting topics but honestly little point in going to class. She puts all notes on blackboard and after the first exam she gave us a list of all the questions on the test. I failed first exam, aced other two. the difference? I stopped going to class. TAs grade INSANELY hard. Honestly, MEMORIZE THE READINGS because that is what they grade on.

She is an awesome teacher. Even if ur major does not require this class, take it. you will be very inspired. her tests are very easy thanks to her review questions. the papers are also very easy and she will look at as many drafts as you want her to. she will go out of her way to help you any way she can. she rocks!!!

analysis.name: Earl Brooks
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Nice enough but not very passionate. Leaves us to our own devices and pretty much has us teach the class so I haven't really learned anything from him. The projects are easy enough once you get past the vagueness. A lot of reading and the readings are sometimes redundant. Don't skip more than 2 classes because he doesnt take drs. notes

Dr. Brooks runs his classes on the premise that students are adults who are responsible for their own education. If you put in the effort, you will learn so much. He is always ready to help with and discuss anything, from his own coursework, to outside projects, to future plans. Don't waste his time if you want to just coast through school:)

Good professor, but can come off unprepared or underwhelming at times. He will start the semester off very tough-sounding, saying that you can't make up work that you miss, but that will change by the end of the semester. Lots of videos, lots of reading. He does not grade ANYTHING until after the semester is over, except attendance.

Professor Brooks was encouraging, he wants best for his students. In class discussions he is considerate in his responses in a refreshing and engaging way. Grades are slow to come back on assignments (mostly of reading responses, essays, and small quizzes) but he gives feedback & is accommodating and willing to help & explain.
He is so disorganized. His instructions are unclear and indirect. I cannot stand his teaching style. I would never take another class with him again.

analysis.name: Ealick Greg
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor was my first encounter with philosophy and he made sure to make it an awesome one. His lectures were never boring and I found them really interesting, plus the were easy to follow which is nice. We only had 2 short papers and one 5-page paper, and they were both easy. If you need to take a philosophy class, make it this one.

Was a little entertaining in class, but super arrogant. I emailed him that I was sick a day in advance, and gives me a zero for it. I go talk to him about it, and he fails to mention there being a pop quiz or anything and refuses to change the grade.
By far the best teacher that I've had so far.  An engergetic teacher who makes the lessons interesting and comprehensible.  Highly recommended.

Ealick is the best. He's open about his expectations, grading criteria (not a pushover), and really knows his stuff. He'll clarify, answer questions, listen if there is an issue, and cares if you care. Attendance is not mandatory but recommended; take good notes. Top notch lectures and discussion is encouraged. I'll never forget this class.

Lots of simple, busy work! Three papers that can be completed with last-minute research, weekly blogs, and three-question quizzes every week. It's not necessary to be present. Overall, a simple elective.

analysis.name: Paul Eagle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Eagle is still an active PR professional, so he is able to really teach about the field with current trends in mind. You turn in 10 "Sharing Stories" over the course of the semester, take a relatively easy mid-term, and then pitch a PR plan with a group for your final. If you're interested in PR, this is a must-take class with a great professor.

Super kind, 
Super chill,
Super interactive.
If you just show up and do the bare minimum you'll get an A.
You could probably do neither of those and still get an A. 
But he's cool and his class is worth attending. 
Highly recommend.

A really sweet guy. He was extremely laid back and so understandable. His class is a public relations class, so he has you bring in a typed paper about a news story you found interesting and has you talk about it in class. One, REALLY easy midterm, which he gives a study guide for and a final group project. Take this if you're an MCS major.

A pretty easy class. you learn a lot of interesting things, but the book isn't necessary to get a good grade. 10 short news stories, a news release, a midterm, then a final project is all you really do. However, make sure you get a good project group or your grade will suffer. Overall a really good professor, very kind and open minded!

Professor Eagle was a great PR professor. As a current professional, he was able to give the class an insider view of what it is like to work in Public Relations. He brought in great guest speakers, and helped us stay current with media trends, something someone in the industry would likely do. Great professor!

analysis.name: William Echlin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's a nice teacher and has a lot of knowledge about many different languages. You have to work hard in this class but he gives you many chances to get extra points(group work).  I'm glad I took this class with him.

class: programming languages. all group work. different language every time, couldn't use c++, java, or python so had to learn new stuff. new project every week. Went above and beyond, explaining everything from how to write a resume, functional programming, chomsky grammars,  and other great theory stuff. also very entertaining.
He is very good. Ask for anything and he will help. Projects every week. Even your midterm and final is a project. Do work and you will get an Easy A in this class.

analysis.name: Edward Orser
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: You know, he is a really nice man. His class is required for the major and he really is NOT a difficult grader. He hands out study guides before each quiz and paper and the guides HAVE THE QUIZ QUESTIONS ON IT. If you are too lazy to pick up a book, change your major.  The only negative thing about him is he rambles and is VERY boring.

FYS on "Sense of Place", had to read a few fiction novels and write papers on them and on "field trips" we went on for the class. It made my days more interesting, at least. Teacher is a sweet old man, he remembers me now and boosted my self esteem concerning my writing. I'd recommend him.

Dr. Orser, though sometimes difficult in personality and grading, is really interested in the progress of his students as well as the quality of your work.  He's also filled with a wealth of useful knowledge and if you make the effort you will learn a LOT from him.

Really nice guy. First part of the class is boring- lewis and Clark. But at the end we got into the environmental movement and was a lot better. Gives study guides but grades a little hard. Not an easy A but if you work a little hard you'll get one.

Great, nice guy, but a horrendously difficult grader.  His grading policy is devastatingly unclear and costs the student the most.  Good for the lectures, but be aware that the papers are killer and plentiful!

analysis.name: Edward Larkey
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Spent a whole class counting his "um"s. It was a 1hr 15 min class and he said "um" 189 times. Went off syllabus first class. Makes up assignments and doesn't give specifics (compare these two shows. that's it). Drones on and on. classes are spent watching the same scene of a show in different languages. Never gives assignments or grades back.

Loves to hear himself talk. Takes attendance when no one is paying attention. Expects you to do the readings when he rarely brings them up in class. There was 1 quiz. Never updates Blackboard. LOTS OF GROUP PAPERS! The premise of the class is awesome but he ruins it with ill-prepared and long lectures. Doesn't stick to syllabus at all. Can't teach.

When walking into this course I thought that the class would be easy. Which in fact the course was. He rarely went off the syllabus or used the books he said to purchas. However, at the end once grades were out the grade DID NOT reflect the other grades that were given during the course of the semester.

Larkey is just winging it the whole time. His lectures go long, and he often repeats his video examples multiple times. The textbook is mostly unrelated to the course in its entirety. He gave one massive quiz that was a solid L. He often goes off syllabus to assign something huge and extensive. The class is interesting, but he's bad at running it.

Larkey is just not a reliable or dependable professor. He doesnt explain assignments well, and the assignments he gives are incredibly convoluted so explanations are very important. He is slow to email back, if he even responds. And he is always unprepared, his lectures are very repetitive and overall pointless. The textbook isnt used at all.

analysis.name: Greg Ealick
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 105 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ealick is really funny and his lectures are interesting. He's disorganized, but he makes up for it in lecture. There are quizzes in discussion, 2 short papers, and 1 long final paper. Never go on your phone or interrupt him (especially when he's about to get to the point). Still participate and ask questions; he's interested in everyone's thoughts.

Aside from the interesting material, this class was awful. The professor is rather arrogant and is terrible about posting grades when he says he will. I still haven't gotten back my last exam despite him saying that he'd have it up over 2 weeks ago. He's passionate about philosophy but his snapping at students and lack of returning emails ruined it

Professor Ealick is a charismatic individual. He makes lots of jokes, yet some come off as needlessly edgy or crude. Nonetheless, he is very passionate about the material. If you show up and do the readings, you can pass easily. Strict on grading, and exams would have no scores higher than a 92 but none lower than a 70. Randomly gives quizzes.

Professor Ealick is genuinely knowledgable about philosophy. He jumps around a bit when giving lectures, but overall wants to make sure his students understand the material. This class is worth taking, but make sure to read over your notes before each class. Ealick is unfair in terms of pop quizzes and if you aren't prepared, it'll knock your grade

This is my first semester at UMBC, and prof. Ealick is one of my favorites! His lectures are always very interesting; never a dull moment. There are easy weekly quizzes in discussion, 2 short writing assignments, and 1 final paper. BE-FRIEND THE TA to get a good grade. His class sparked an interest in philosophy in me that I never thought I had.

analysis.name: Edward Rudow
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: No papers, no assignments, no quizzes. Just two take-home tests (midterm & final). Rambles on and on in class, but you should have a computer to waste time on while he does so. Easiest A at the campus. Also, buy the e-book for his classes if available. Makes it easier to find the answers for the tests. Attendance is mandatory though, get the points

This man is a gem in the broken world of academia. His class was exceptionally easy, but I still learned more from him than any other professor. Other sections had a 20+ page final; we had a 2 page final. Take him because if he taught every class in the program, I would take him over anyone else, any day of the week.

Dr Rudow is great. Class discussions are engaging & helpful in understanding concepts.  Exams are take home, for someone who suffers from exam anxiety, extremely grateful! I learned a lot minus the anxiety that surrounds exams. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
BEST professor everrr. His test are take home, and he argues the answers when you "turn them in," which means you hand your test to your friend and they grade it. He's so chill and funny. LOVE HIM!

He's so chill but reads off PPT slides. He's basically reiterating what's in the book. You will complete several assessments on your personality, etc. and write a paper on your findings about yourself. Pretty fun.  Midterm  3 ppg. take home, cover 3 units/chaps. on most important things you learned. There's a presentation (1-3 people) and a paper.

analysis.name: Charles Eggleton
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He was nice, we barely met because it was online but he was easy going and a good teacher. He knew the material well and knew how to teach it. He wasnt so tech savy which was annoying but it was bearable. His exams were hard but he was a fair grader.
Dr. Eggleton is a sweetheart and an excellent professor. Fluids is one of the hardest classes so you still need to put in a lot of work to pass.

Most irritating teacher I've ever had. His monotone voice and repeated use off the word "right?" every two seconds drove me up the wall. Horrible instructor, does not like to teach. Uses a reversed classroom, which means that you teach yourself and he stares blankly at you while you do problems in class.

he s a very nice professor. he ll explain things clearly if you ask him questions. quizzes and exams are mostly from homework, so make sure you study every problem. he curves your grade by giving you a chance to use final exam grade to replace your worst midterm grade. it saved most ppl.

Word of advice when taking this class: learn how to do Kline-McClintock error analysis, and show ALL of your formulas in the Appendix section, or else he'll brutalize your papers. Also, he lies about giving necessary equations on the final exam, so memorize them in advance.

analysis.name: David Eisenmann
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 69 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Never opened my book--just go through his lectures and the audio after class and you should have no problem getting an A in the course. All his exams are straight out of the powerpoint. He does a great job explaining it clearly. He's one of the best professors I've had. The last exam was quite difficult, but other than that it's not too bad.

Just took the most recent exam, and I'm honestly losing hope in this class. The practice exams and clickers are NOTHING like the exams. No learning objectives except to practically inhale all of his slides but then on the exam you realize the slides were useless because reading through his exam will take half the time. Discussion is the worst.

Let me start by saying you can tell dude man is smart and knows his area well. But as a student starting that class I don't. 302 is hard enough already without him flying through lectures and leaving his PowerPoint slides blank so you constantly have to look and see if you have to snap a picture or not. Not gonna say avoid him but hes not easy

I took the class with Dr. B and E. The class is very difficult. The first few weeks may be review, but after that there are a lot of small details. He speaks very fast and does not post the slides in full online. I just listened to his lectures again because he spoke so fast. I pretty much barely got an A with the curve(I got lucky).

I struggle with this class. I'm coming here after taking exam 2 so things may change. But currently, I don't like the structure of exams. It did not reflect the practice exams. They are so long and dense with info. And sometimes the answer choices are very similar, you have to know the specific details. Plus, hw and ICAs are one attempt. This sucks

analysis.name: . Eisenman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors in UMBC! Knows the subject very well, answers questions clearly, helpful and welcoming during office hours. Exams are fair nothing tricky. CPS questions and the questions from the back of the book Dr. Eisenmann suggests at the beginning of each lecture very helpful for exams! Go to class, understand cps questions study!

Eisenmann is definitely an expert in his field. He is very knowledgeable in his lectures so definitely pay attention. Genetics is not an easy class but he tries his best to help you. The clickers are the KEY to his exams. Very understanding and empathetic with his students.

Great professor. Excellent, detailed slides, relevant cps questions (very similar to exam questions). Very good speaker and answers questions precisely (not like certain other professors also teaching 302 who never answer the darn question).
Super clear lectures and is willing to engage with students during them! The homework and clickers can be difficult but the tests are pretty clearly based on lecture material.
Excellent Professor! Really known his stuff and wants everyone to do well. Goes a little fast buts posts lectures on Itunes. Would definitely take him again

analysis.name: Stuart Eisenman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is one of the most ridiculously easy classes I have ever had!  The teacher is a nice guy, but he doesn't teach anything.  I don't think he does any preparation work for the class at all (I don't think he has even read the book).  He makes up for this by giving open note exams, which, again, makes this class a total joke.

The class is very easy. Just show up, listen to him go over the slides, and then leave.  Even though he moves at a very fast pace (a chapter a class), it's very basic and general.  If you have basic accounting knowledge, you'll be fine.  Ask for take-home tests and open-note tests, he'll more than likely will give it to you.

Easy class. Good Professor! A day before the exam he will go over what will be on it. If you study from that you'll be fine. Learn a lot from this class. WOrk load: 4-5 exams (easy), 1 project, 1 oral presentation. Very good Professor.

Read the book, you'll need it for this class. People say this is easy class, if might if you actually do the work and read the text. It's not easy as it looks, as half of our class drop. Anyway, great professor.
Yeah I already knew some accounting coming in and he had no idea what he's talking about. Read the book and you'll be fine. Nice guy, just doesnt prepare at all for class lol.

analysis.name: Mary Ely Hernandez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is amazing with helping students understand Spanish. Very participation-oriented but she makes sure the discussion is fun and engaging. Assignments are completed online, and while they're a bit tedious they're not difficult. Exams can be tricky. Overall Prof Hernandez challenges her classes but makes sure they succeed if they try.

She is honestly an amazing teacher! I had her for SPAN101 and then a different teacher for SPAN102 and the differences in their teaching styles were insane. Prof Hernandez is very patient and understanding when it comes to questions. She is a big fan of class participation, which actually helps with her conversational style of teaching.

Mary Ely is so sweet and cares so much about her students. Participation is important, but she fosters a forgiving classroom. She's very encouraging and super helpful, and while there's homework at least a couple times a week, as long as you actually try, you can't fail. She's the best Spanish teacher here and she actually wants you to learn.

Professor Hernandez was very caring. There is a lot of homework, but if you do them little by little over time it becomes more manageable. She is very understanding that most students haven't taken Spanish in a long time. She is very kind and helpful, she tells you exactly what will be on written/oral exams so you can prepare. Def take her class!

There are assignments every class. You can access them online, but she will not accept submissions unless you were in class. I already speak spanish, but this class is not really beginner friendly. Since day one, she was adding spanish into her vocab. A classmate of mine struggled a lot and decided to drop out. Way too many assignments tbh.

analysis.name: Elaine MacDougall
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Elaine is an incredible professor. College is meant to push us to grow and she creates a warm space to learn and experiment with ideas. She won't force you to learn, that's your own responsibility and why you're in college, but if you put in the effort you'll become a more fully formed human:)

Professor MacDougall is such a kind and lovely person. The course was an honors seminar, so it was discussion based and there were projects included but there were no exams. She is so understanding and so genuine, she made the course engaging. I would 100% recommend you take her class!
I took a class with her back in 2013 and I still remember how great of a professor she was for ENGL100 Composition. Definitely take her class if you get the chance!

Elaine is my favorite professor ever. She is so caring and understanding towards students, and doesn't make her classes more difficult than they need to be. If you have the chance to take a class with Elaine, absolutely take it.

Took the FYS - Truth and Technology, and it was super chill and actually pretty fun! She was a really good professor and very understanding. The assignments we had were all easy and she wasn't too bad about deadlines either. Definitely the easiest A for me for the semester. If I was able to take english with I would've! She's an amazing prof!!!

analysis.name: Liz Stanwyck
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I loved Dr. Stanwyck. Stat is a really hard class in general but she makes it bearable and pretty understandable. She always tries to explain the best she can and is so willing to answer your questions. Super nice and adds 10 points to tests for a little boost.

Loved her! She really made sure everyone knew what was going on in class. She explained concepts well and made it easy to understand. And she's super animated in a way that makes you want to keep learning calculus. There were 3 exams (including the final) and 3 projects. You can skip lecture but attend discussion and seminar because they count!

Great professor! It was her first time teaching STAT 350 and she was amazing. I didn't really like the format of the class but her teaching was great. You can tell she really cares and that is something you don't see in a lot of professors at UMBC sadly. I had a great semester with her! Even though she doesn't curve or anything class was still okay

Prof Stanwyck is an awesome professor. Statistics isn't my strong suit but she was always very understanding and accessible, and had a great sense of humor. She was always very engaging and you can tell she loves what she teaches.

Absolutely an amazing teacher! Accessible outside of class via Discord. Promptly answered questions w/ supporting info/examples to give a better understanding. You can tell she's passionate about the class, making it more inviting and easier to learn. Drops the 3 lowest quiz and hw scores. A difficult class in general but she makes it tolerable.

analysis.name: Emily Yoon
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
-Class was actually English 204-
 It is an English class, there will be reading but most of the semester was poems/short essays and stories so it wasn't over the top. We did finish with a novel but it was a very quick read and a very good book. The reading material Dr. Yoon picked was always interesting and she obviously cares about her students.

Prof. Perez is an exemplary & visionary educator. I appreciate & treasure everything she has taught me. Enjoyed the class & learned so much from it. Having her encouragement & support even when I wanted to give up was invaluable. Her class was one of the highlights of my week - each one brought something new and exciting to learn & think about.

She makes you work for the writing-intensive requirement. 500-word responses weekly, 3 essays, group project. She's strict on grading but gives you plenty of feedback and workshop. Most classes are discussions on readings each day, participation graded. She does a checkpoint halfway through to let you know how you're doing. Overall good professor.

Dr Perez is awesome! She gives lots of constructive feedback on papers & writes a personal response to every discussion post, so you can tell she really engages with everyone's work. Classes are discussion-based but she never forces you to speak. She also lets you skip a few discussion weeks which is helpful for when you have a really busy week.

Close to if not a perfect professor. Her readings are never excessive, and she gives meaningful feedback to every assignment including the small ones. You'll read new, interesting, and engaging texts, and there is rarely a dull moment in the class. You will not regret taking her. Talk to her too, she is such a lovely person and is super helpful.

analysis.name: Emmanuel Keravec
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: truly my goat, funny guy that offers a good, difficult class that teaches a lot of important subjects.

Prof. Keravec is an accomplished writer in the field of writing for media arts. However, he does not do the best job teaching the class. He has a well of knowledge of the industry of writing and developing writing, but he does not explain concepts nor point students into the direction of fully understanding them. He also seldom responds to emails.

He's a pretty good teacher. The class is like an open discussion and you help edit and give suggestions to each others work throughout the semester. Lots of homework, but it isn't awful. You'll rarely receive a 20/20 on an assignment, but his feedback is helpful and he wants his students to succeed. I would recommend this class !!

analysis.name: Emmanuel Anoruo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This man gets my vote for "worst professor ever". He  is unable to explain some of the most fundamental economic concepts, and is bad at explaining those he does understand. The best thing about his 312 is the text; Mankiw is excellent. He is very biased, and his lectures consist of reading Mankiw's PPT slides. He takes attendance. Awful.

His class is easy, then he gives you his test. The first test was missing a chapter that he told us to prepare for, and that we spent most of class time going over, and had problems from a section we were not told to prepare for. The second test about 20 people were still there 35 minutes after class was supposed to be over still struggling to end

Dr. Anoruo is a very helpful professor.  Although at times his explanations may be confusing, he does his best to make the class doable.  He assigns and grades homework, and says on the first day of class that he will not try to make anything difficult for the students.  He even gave a take home exam for the class.  He's also a really nice guy.

Econ 312 in itself it a difficult subject to take at UMBC and if you can get an easy A with Anoruo then do it! I will take any class this guy teaches because it leaves more time to study for other more complex classes like Advanced Accounting. Take him with anything if you want an easy A. No thought process was involved in this class at all.

BEST TEACHER EVER! If you fail his class, there must be something seriously wrong with you. He tells you exactly what he wants on his exams (gives you practice exams). He takes attendance so you would want to go. What I love about him is that he explains everything step by step. Best teacher.

analysis.name: Emily Erickson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
